_meta.purpose: Oracle capture of CapCut UI output for a 3-keyframe Cubic Out triplet, used to lock the byte-identity contract of cmdAddKeyframe.
capcut_capture_steps: Created 3 scale_x keyframes at t=0/5s/8.133s with scale 1.0/1.3/1.0.
Applied 'Cubic Out' preset via right-click on each of the 3 keyframes (forcing CapCut to recompute the Bezier handles for the new intervals).
Saved and read draft_content.json raw bytes.

intervals_microseconds.note: Segment 0→1 is frame-aligned at 60fps (5M μs = 300 frames). Segment 1→2 is NOT frame-aligned: -0.4 × 3_133_333 = -1_253_333.2 and +0.32 × 3_133_333 = 1_002_666.56, both with non-integer fractions. CapCut's rounding on non-aligned intervals is not strictly floor or round — see expectations.tolerance_microseconds.

expectations.y_tolerance_rationale: CapCut's y = 0.94 × Δscale is computed in C++ doubles with its own rounding; v1.3.0 computes Math.round(0.94 × Δscale × 1e6) / 1e6. For 'clean' Δscale (e.g. ±0.5 → ±0.47) results are bit-identical; for 'ugly' Δscale (e.g. ±0.3 → ±0.282) the two implementations land on adjacent IEEE 754 doubles (1 ULP apart, ~5e-17). This is below any conceivable rendering tolerance and is documented as part of the byte-identity contract.
